title: Phosphoribosyltransferase with unusual pyrimidine specificity involved in 5-azacytidine biosynthesis
content: We recently identified a gene cluster responsible for the biosynthesis of 5-azacytidine (1), which is a cytidine-mimic nucleoside with a unique base moiety, 5-azacytosine (2). We also revealed that 2 was biosynthesized from guanosine-5′-triphosphate (GTP) by three enzymes, AzcE, AzcA, and AzcB/C. However, the pathway for the biosynthesis of 1 from 2 remains unknown. In this study, we examined the remaining biosynthetic steps including the ribosylation step. We first examined whether AzcD catalyzes the ribosylation of 2 because AzcD shows sequence similarity to type I phosphoribosyltransferases. In vitro analysis showed that AzcD catalyzed the phosphoribosylation of 2 to form 5′-monophosphorylated 1 (3) with phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate (4). The enzyme also accepted cytosine but not uracil. To the best of our knowledge, AzcD is the first phosphoribosyltransferase accepting cytosine as a substrate, highlighting its unusual pyrimidine specificity. A search of the Protein Data Bank for homologs using XtalPred identified uracil phosphoribosyltransferases (UPRTs). Comparison with UPRTs and docking simulations with 4 and either 2 or cytosine suggested that an altered hydrogen-bonding geometry for recognition of the pyrimidine base may contribute to the distinct substrate specificity of AzcD. We also showed that recombinant AzcG catalyzed the hydrolysis of the 5′-phosphate group of 3 to yield 1. Together, these results reveal the final steps of 5-azacytidine biosynthesis and demonstrate diversification of pyrimidine recognition in a UPRT-like phosphoribosyltransferase.
